# The Empire

The ruling order. It has no ratified name (Q-0002); "the empire" and "the keeps" serve
as working references, and THE PLENTY (D-0132) names its legal-economic
framework (`data/lexicon.yaml`).

## What the antagonist is

> status: ratified (D-0010, D-0011, D-0013, D-0033)

There is no idiosyncratic demon king — that was explicitly rejected. The antagonist is
a system: the disease of greed, expressed through incentives that make ordinary people
do monstrous things. The rich poisoned the world and keep poisoning it; the ones who
suffer are the ones downstream. Everyone lives inside the machine of it: bailiffs hit
quotas so their own children eat; villages inform on strangers to buy leniency on the
winter tax; miners defend the mine that is killing them because it is the only wage.
The setting is not grimdark — but it is a bad, bad place that pulls people toward bad
choices, and the story shows the pull, in a wide range of grays.

## The modern mirrors (authors'-room only)

> status: ratified (D-0019, D-0030)

The design guides for the antagonist class are the modern billionaire, the fascist
bureaucracy, the extractive corporation, and the runaway optimizing system of the
corporatist-AI wasteland — a post-imperial power in decay. None of this vocabulary
ever surfaces in-world: on the page and in the ear it is lords, keeps, scribes,
tithes, and parchment, fully readable as pure fantasy.

## The framework: the Plenty

> status: ratified (D-0132)

The framework's in-world name is **the Plenty** — the singularity doublespeak
realized (D-0131): a name that promises abundance, rest, and provision, naming the
system that unmakes the worth of a person's work. Said in nearly every episode;
sayable in dread and in irony alike. "The Iron Ledger" is retired as the framework's
name and survives only as a possible in-world
phrase for the ledgers themselves.

## The framework's working model

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The working model: the empire's true sovereign is its own accumulated law — a
centuries-deep, self-perpetuating web of quotas, tithes, and binding fictions that
even the great lords serve. Fail your numbers and the system discards you, lord and
serf alike. The elite are not free; they are the machine's best-fed prisoners, and
most of them are terrified. This is what "no demon king" looks like in practice: the
throne is a ledger.

## Keeps, scriptoriums, and the insulation of the high

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The keeps are the elite's fortress-granaries — high, warded, provisioned — where the
consequences of extraction never reach. Inside them, scriptoriums of low-caste scribes
grind out the empire's paperwork and absorb the cognitive damage of maintaining its
contradictions. The higher the rank, the cleaner the hands, the further from the mud.
The endgame rumor of the elite: sealed, perfected keeps to outlast the collapse they
are causing — the world made small enough to hoard.

## The Tithe of Minds

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The empire's most intimate extraction: periodic sweeps that test peripheral children
for unusual gifts and take the brightest to be trained as living calculators. It is
how the protagonist was taken ([[protagonists-taking]]), how native lines of teaching
are cut, and why hiding a gifted child is one of the commonest crimes of love in the
world ([[information-control]]).

## Enclosure as method

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The empire's founding move and its daily one: fence a commons, declare it separate,
back the fiction with law and force, and let the resulting debt fall on those outside
the fence ([[first-storehouse-lie]], [[pre-history]]). Every generation encloses
something new — pastures, rivers, looms, words, minds — because the Ledger's numbers
must grow.

## The faces of it

> status: proposed

Sketched, unratified: the exhausted checkpoint bailiff with his abacus and his sick
daughter; the arch-scribes who genuinely believe their arithmetic is civilization;
inquisitor-auditors who hunt "inefficiency" like heresy; the pallid keep-aristocracy
trading their own daughters between towers. See [[secondary-archetypes]] for the
worked examples and Q-0015 for their unratified names.

## The elite are not monolithic
> status: ratified (D-0093)

The ruling body is not a single bloc with a single will. Its internal politics are a
required part of the picture: distinct elements inside the elite pulling against one
another, each with its own aims, fears, and rivalries. This follows directly from the
"no demon king" principle (D-0010, D-0033) — a system, not a villain, and systems have
seams. Whatever factions are eventually canonized, the requirement stands that the keeps
contend among themselves.

## Sketched internal factions
> status: proposed

Unratified sketch of four currents within the elite (all names AI-coined, placeholders
pending the naming oracle and Q-0002):

- **The Chalk Lords** — decadent inheritor-shareholders who demand thicker wards and
  ever-higher quotas to fund the luxury of their sealed keeps; the billionaire-bunker
  class of the [[allegory]].
- **The Iron Actuaries** — algorithm-purist master scribes who blame the world's
  imperfection rather than their own arithmetic, dream of formatting the continent
  clean, and quietly plot against the lords they serve.
- **The Silver Bough** — paternalistic green-reformers who would patent the cure:
  broken-in, docile spirits and cloned soil sold back to a poisoned world. They are
  framed as the protagonist's darkest mirror — her equal in raw bandwidth, her opposite
  in politics: a top-down proprietary fix against her open, teaching one.
- **The Vellum Hounds** — the enforcers, Pinkerton-style, often class-traitor laborers
  paid in rations; the resentment seam runs here, in bodies spent as disposable shields
  by the very lords they protect ([[information-control]]).

Which of these currents made the protagonist is no longer open — see "The protagonist's
makers" below (D-0124). The Iron Actuaries and the Silver Bough are thereby ratified in
function (their existence and role are canon); the Chalk Lords and Vellum Hounds remain
proposed sketches, and all four names stay oracle-pending (Q-0002).

## The protagonist's makers
> status: ratified (D-0124)

Taken from outside by the Tithe of Minds, she was first trained in raw calculation by the Iron
Actuaries — so the empire's arithmetic is her mother tongue — and then claimed and raised by
the Silver Bough, the paternalistic green-reformers who would patent the cure. The Bough is her
equal-in-bandwidth dark mirror (open teaching against proprietary fix, the D-0029 allegory),
and her recurring, sympathetic-but-wrong elite antagonist is a Bough figure who loved her and
believes, with real sincerity, that they are the real good guys — one who keeps offering to
bring her back to fix the world their way. She carries both inheritances: Actuary arithmetic and Bough
Wyrd-healing. Inside her Archive the enemy-within is an arch-scribe Actuary ([[protagonist]],
D-0120); her living antagonist is a Bough — the seam of the elite's own politics running
straight through one woman (D-0093). The faction names remain oracle-pending (Q-0002).

## Frankpledge

> status: provisional (D-0145)

The empire binds the parishes in frankpledge: every tithing-member answerable for
every other, so that a neighbour's failure is your fine and a neighbour's flight is
your debt. On parchment it reads as care — none may fall alone; in practice it is
the cheapest surveillance ever devised, a cage whose bars are the people themselves.
The resistance does not break the institution; it re-lays it. Where the keeps built
mutual liability, the parishes quietly practice mutual aid — the same bond, read
from the other side ([[allegory]], the reclamation move in institutional form). The
specific workings (tithing sizes, the oath, how a parish turns the ledger of blame
into a ledger of care) remain to be written.
